title: Kubernetes Networking: CNI, Services, Ingress & Gateway API
summary: Master cloud-native Kubernetes networking: CNI packet encapsulation, ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer and Headless Services, CoreDNS discovery, NetworkPolicies, and Gateway API routing.
learningObjectives: Design and configure Kubernetes service discovery mechanisms with ClusterIP, Headless Services, and CoreDNS SRV records.
Enforce zero-trust network perimeter isolation utilizing namespace-wide default-deny NetworkPolicies and fine-grained pod selector ingress rules.
Implement modern cloud-native ingress architecture utilizing Gateway API resources (GatewayClass, Gateway, HTTPRoute) alongside traditional Ingress controllers.

curriculumModules.title: CNI Network Model & Pod-to-Pod Communication
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: The Container Network Interface (CNI) enforces that every Pod receives a unique, routable IP address across nodes without NAT. Overlay networks (VXLAN, Geneve) and routed networks (BGP, Calico, Cilium eBPF) manage encapsulation and wire-speed routing.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Deploy eBPF-based CNI (Cilium) to bypass iptables overhead at scale (10,000+ services) and enable kernel-level Socket-level load balancing (kube-proxy replacement).

curriculumModules.title: Service Discovery, Kube-Proxy & CoreDNS Internals
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Kubernetes Services provide stable virtual IPs (ClusterIP) abstracting dynamic pod endpoints. Headless services (clusterIP: None) return direct pod A/AAAA and SRV records via CoreDNS for stateful peer discovery.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Tune CoreDNS cache plugins, autoscaling (DNS horizontal autoscaler), and configure ndots:2 in pod dnsConfig to eliminate excessive search domain lookup penalties.

curriculumModules.title: Zero-Trust NetworkPolicies & Modern Gateway API
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: NetworkPolicies operate as distributed packet filters at Layer 3/4. The modern Gateway API succeeds Ingress with role-oriented abstractions (GatewayClass for infra, Gateway for cluster ops, HTTPRoute for app developers).
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Enforce a default-deny ingress and egress NetworkPolicy across all production namespaces as a baseline, whitelisting only explicit DNS (UDP 53) and verified inter-service dependencies.

labs.productionContext: Stateful and distributed microservices require both virtual IP load-balanced endpoints (ClusterIP) for client queries and headless DNS SRV discovery for peer clustering.

labs.title: Zero-Trust NetworkPolicies & Modern Gateway API Route Filtering
labs.scenario: Harden namespace net-policy with a default-deny ingress NetworkPolicy, permit authorized ingress traffic on port 80 to checkout-api pods, and configure a modern Gateway API HTTPRoute routing /checkout traffic through edge-gateway.
labs.productionContext: Zero-trust compliance mandates denying all lateral East-West traffic by default, while modern North-South ingress utilizes declarative Gateway API HTTPRoutes instead of legacy Ingress annotations.
objectives: Create namespace net-policy for secured workloads

validationRules.name: checkout-route
validationRules.remediation: Set rule match path to /checkout in checkout-route.

solutionCommands:
echo -e "apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-ingress
  namespace: net-policy
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress" > /home/learner/default-deny.yaml

echo -e "apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-checkout-ingress
  namespace: net-policy
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: checkout-api
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80" > /home/learner/allow-checkout.yaml

echo -e "apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: checkout-route
  namespace: net-policy
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - name: edge-gateway
  rules:
  - matches:
    - path:
        type: PathPrefix
        value: /checkout
    backendRefs:
    - name: checkout-api
      port: 80" > /home/learner/checkout-route.yaml
labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure namespace net-policy exists, default-deny and allow-checkout NetworkPolicies are applied, and checkout-route HTTPRoute matches /checkout.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the primary difference in DNS resolution between a standard ClusterIP Service and a Headless Service (clusterIP: None)?
options: (Recommended) A standard ClusterIP returns a single virtual IP load-balanced across pods, whereas a Headless Service returns multiple A/AAAA records with direct individual Pod IP addresses and SRV records.
A Headless Service disables DNS resolution completely, requiring hardcoded IP addresses.
A standard ClusterIP Service cannot route traffic across nodes, while a Headless Service routes externally.
A Headless Service requires an external LoadBalancer cloud controller to generate IP addresses.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Headless Services (clusterIP: None) do not allocate a virtual ClusterIP; instead, CoreDNS resolves the service domain name directly to the set of individual Pod IPs backing the selector, which is critical for stateful clustering, peer discovery, and client-side load balancing.

assessmentQuestions.question: In the Kubernetes Gateway API architecture, which persona and resource is responsible for defining application traffic routing rules to backend services?
options: (Recommended) Application Developers configure HTTPRoute or GRPCRoute resources attached to parent Gateways.
Infrastructure Providers configure GatewayClass resources on the worker nodes.
Cluster Operators configure HTTPRoute resources inside the kube-system namespace.
Linux kernel administrators write eBPF programs inside the CNI daemonset.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: The Gateway API uses role-oriented resource separation: Infrastructure Providers manage GatewayClass, Cluster Operators deploy Gateway listeners, and Application Developers author HTTPRoute or GRPCRoute manifests attached to parent Gateways to control layer 7 traffic routing.
